title: Next Palindrome Using Same Digits
summary: Given a numeric string representing a palindrome, find the smallest palindrome larger than the input by rearranging its digits.
statement: Given a numeric string representing a palindrome, find the smallest palindrome larger than the input by rearranging its digits. Return an empty string if no such palindrome exists.
constraints: num is already a palindrome and contains only decimal digits.
Rearrange the same digits into the smallest strictly larger palindrome, or return an empty string if impossible.
reference_solution:
def next_larger_palindrome(num):
 digits=list(num);half=len(digits)//2;pivot=half-2
 while pivot>=0 and digits[pivot]>=digits[pivot+1]:pivot-=1
 if pivot<0:return ''
 successor=half-1
 while digits[successor]<=digits[pivot]:successor-=1
 digits[pivot],digits[successor]=digits[successor],digits[pivot]
 digits[pivot+1:half]=reversed(digits[pivot+1:half])
 for index in range(half):digits[-1-index]=digits[index]
 return ''.join(digits)

hints: A palindrome is determined completely by its first half and optional center digit.
Find the next lexicographic permutation of the first half.
Swap the rightmost ascent pivot with its smallest larger suffix digit, reverse the suffix, then mirror.
Next-permutation produces the smallest larger half; mirroring preserves all digits and order comparison, so it produces the smallest larger palindrome.

tests.explanation: The next permutation of the first half 12 is 21, which mirrors to 2112.
The first half 32 has no larger permutation, so no larger palindrome exists.
